 NAND Flash Prices Set to Decline in 2027 as Chinese CSP Order Cuts Outweigh North American Demand Growth, Says TrendForce
 19 November 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce’s latest memory industry research indicates that the global NAND Flash market is expected to see a reversal in supply-demand dynamics in 2027. With supply set to grow rapidly, substantial cuts to enterprise SSD orders from Chinese CSPs—coupled with a potential further contraction in consumer electronics demand—are expected to exacerbate oversupply. 
 TrendForce forecasts that the overall NAND Flash contract prices will begin declining in the first quarter of 2027, with quarterly price drops potentially widening as the year progresses.
 TrendForce estimates that global NAND Flash industry CapEx will increase 26.7% YoY to US$29.9 billion in 2027.
 Strong demand for high-performance storage in North America continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade process technology. Meanwhile, rising QLC penetration and the transition to higher-layer-count NAND technologies will further boost bit output. Although some suppliers may slightly slow their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, global NAND Flash bit supply is still projected to grow by somewhere between 25–30% YoY in 2027.
 Enterprise SSDs remain the primary growth driver for the NAND Flash industry, but regional demand trends are increasingly diverging. In North America, U.S.-based CSPs have recently raised their 2027 demand forecasts again, supported by AI agent and general-purpose server projects already under construction. 
 Chinese CSPs, however, are facing challenges including GPU shortages, elevated inventory levels, and intensifying competition over token pricing. As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by an amount that exceeds the additional demand from U.S.-based CSPs.
 In the consumer market, inventories of low-cost memory are expected to be depleted in 2027, putting upward pressure on finished-device prices and further weighing on shipments. Additionally, brands seeking to control bill-of-materials (BOM) costs will need to reduce storage capacity specifications, resulting in a significant decline in average capacity per device and further widening the demand shortfall.
 NAND Flash prices forecast to fall 0–5% QoQ in 1Q27, with all product categories entering a downward cycle from 2Q27 
 TrendForce notes that continued downward revisions to global consumer electronics shipments, along with reduced enterprise SSD orders in China, have already begun to weigh on NAND Flash contract prices in the fourth quarter of 2026. 
 In response, TrendForce has lowered its forecast for quarterly contract price increases to 8–13%. Weakening demand has also intensified inventory-clearing pressure in distribution channels, triggering a sharp correction of more than 20% in spot prices recently.
 Looking ahead to 2027, cuts to enterprise SSD demand from Chinese CSPs are expected to offset order growth in North America, while supply growth will significantly outpace demand throughout the year. As oversupply intensifies, TrendForce forecasts that overall NAND Flash contract prices will decline by 0–5% QoQ in the first quarter, with all product categories entering a downward price cycle beginning in the second quarter.
 TrendForce emphasizes that the market outlook will depend on the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, changes to restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether consumer electronics manufacturers continue adopting lower memory specifications in 2028. 
 Another key factor will be the direction of US policy following the mid-term election, particularly whether any changes affect major AI data center projects planned for 2028 that are still in the planning and permitting stages. The pace of project approvals and capital expenditure will directly influence advance inventory procurement in the second half of 2027.

 Global OLED Monitor Shipments Double YoY in 3Q26 as Rankings Shift Dramatically Among Top Five Brands, Says TrendForce
 18 November 2026 
 Display 
 /
 Consumer Electronics 
 TrendForce 
 Global OLED monitor shipments maintained strong momentum in the third quarter of 2026, rising 13% QoQ and doubling compared with the same period in 2025, according to TrendForce’s latest research. Growth was driven not only by continued product launches from major brands, which helped boost shipment volumes, but also by ample upstream panel supply. The latter has enabled second-tier and emerging brands to significantly expand their shipments.
 ASUS retains top spot as MSI climbs to second place for the first time 
 TrendForce reports that competition in the OLED monitor market intensified in the third quarter as brands adjusted their strategies and product portfolios. Rankings shifted considerably among the second- through fifth-largest vendors, highlighting the increasingly fierce competition among brands vying for positions just below the market leader.
 Amid this competitive landscape, ASUS maintained its position as the world’s leading OLED monitor brand, capturing a 21.7% market share. Shipments rose a steady 6% QoQ, supported by an easing of supply constraints on its key high-end 27-inch QHD 540Hz panels. The launch of new models commemorating the brand’s 20th anniversary also helped stimulate demand.
 MSI climbed to second place globally for the first time, with its market share increasing 1.7 percentage points QoQ to 14.5%. Its cumulative shipments over the first three quarters were roughly on par with Samsung’s. MSI’s third-quarter growth was primarily driven by increased orders for its 27-inch QHD monitors ahead of the holiday shopping season, alongside the successive launches of several new models, including 27-inch QHD 320Hz monitors.
 Samsung slipped to third place, with its market share declining to 11.3%. Although the company’s shipments remained relatively stable throughout the first three quarters of 2026, its share was diluted by the rapid expansion of the overall market. In response to mounting competition, Samsung plans to ramp up shipments aggressively in the fourth quarter, targeting the year-end holiday shopping season in Europe and North America. This push could help the company reclaim its position as the world's second-largest supplier.
 LGE rose one position to fourth place, securing an 8.6% market share in the third quarter. Aggressive promotional campaigns for select 27-inch QHD 240Hz models successfully stimulated demand and supported the brand’s improved ranking.
 Dell also moved up one position to fifth place, as its shipment performance recovered and its quarterly market share reached 8.2%. Growth was primarily fueled by continued shipment expansion of its mainstream 27-inch QHD 240Hz models, together with accelerating shipments of a new 39-inch model introduced in the second quarter.

 SpaceX’s Adoption of Qualcomm 5G Chipsets Could Significantly Reduce the Cost of Deploying Tens of Thousands of Base Stations, Says TrendForce
 17 November 2026 
 Telecommunications 
 TrendForce 
 SpaceX and Qualcomm recently announced a multi-year supply agreement under which SpaceX will widely adopt Qualcomm’s Dragonwing 5G base station chipset solutions. TrendForce believes the partnership will significantly reduce SpaceX’s base station deployment costs while simplifying system integration across equipment from multiple vendors, thereby accelerating the large-scale commercial rollout of its 5G network.
 TrendForce notes that integrating terrestrial 5G base stations powered by Qualcomm’s Dragonwing platform with a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation compliant with 3GPP Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) standards could effectively address two major limitations of conventional satellite connectivity: link budget losses associated with indoor coverage and capacity constraints in high-density user environments.
 Under this architecture, terrestrial base stations would handle high-density traffic offloading in urban areas while strengthening indoor coverage. Meanwhile, the satellite constellation would provide wide-area connectivity and extend service to coverage gaps. Together, these complementary networks would enable coordinated operation through a space-terrestrial heterogeneous network (ST-HetNet), supporting a comprehensive range of telecommunications services.
 Pre-integrated O-RAN solutions help SpaceX reduce dependence on traditional equipment vendors 
 TrendForce projects the global 5G infrastructure’s market value will reach US$55 billion in 2027, up 24.3% YoY, as 5G applications diversify, subscriber numbers rise, and 5G fixed wireless access (FWA) gains traction. 
 SpaceX is actively expanding into the U.S. mobile communications market, moving away from the proprietary radio access network (RAN) architectures traditionally dominated by telecommunications equipment giants such as Ericsson and Nokia.
 Instead, the company has opted for Qualcomm’s 5G base station chipsets, designed for open RAN (O-RAN) architectures. These solutions enable rapid integration of third-party radio units (RUs) and distributed units (DUs), with interoperability supported by standardized open fronthaul interfaces. This approach could substantially reduce the cost of deploying tens of thousands of 5G base stations across the United States. Another key factor behind SpaceX’s decision to partner with Qualcomm is the chipset platform’s ability to enable seamless integration between terrestrial 5G base stations and satellite backhaul links serving remote areas.
 Traditionally, telecommunications operators deploying O-RAN networks have faced interoperability challenges when sourcing distributed units (DUs), radio units (RUs), and centralized units (CUs) from different equipment manufacturers. This is because variations in vendor implementations can create signal compatibility issues that complicate network integration and slow deployment.
 This time, SpaceX is standardizing its base stations around Qualcomm’s 5G chipset solutions. Qualcomm will complete the integration and interoperability testing of RU-DU fronthaul interfaces before the equipment leaves the factory, helping ensure stable signal transmission during actual network operations. By reducing the complexity of multi-vendor integration, this pre-integrated approach is expected to enable faster and more efficient large-scale network deployment.
 Spectrum acquisitions and tower leasing create new supply chain opportunities 
 Since 2025, SpaceX has progressively acquired a combined 65 MHz of mid-band spectrum from EchoStar, supporting its efforts to expand beyond satellite broadband into direct-to-cell (D2C) connectivity and satellite-enabled vehicle communications.
 In October 2026, the company further strengthened its spectrum portfolio by acquiring critical 800 MHz mobile communications spectrum from Grain Management. Furthermore, SpaceX secured access to approximately 80,000 base station sites through leasing arrangements with independent tower operators, accelerating its push toward commercial mobile communications services in the United States.
 While SpaceX and Qualcomm work together to accelerate the rollout of mobile communications infrastructure, suppliers of 5G base station components are also positioned to gain new business opportunities.
 TrendForce expects established partners within Qualcomm’s ecosystem to be among the primary beneficiaries. Potential suppliers include Amphenol for base station antenna development and Qorvo for power amplifiers (PAs), while American Tower and Crown Castle could provide tower leasing and site infrastructure support.

 Global TV Shipments Decline 3.6% YoY in 3Q26 as Brands Target Premium Mini LED and RGB Mini LED Markets, Says TrendForce
 16 November 2026 
 Consumer Electronics 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce's latest TV industry research indicates that global TV brand shipments regained some momentum in 3Q26 as manufacturers gradually stepped up inventory preparations ahead of the year-end promotional season. 
 Shipments reached 47.94 million units, rising 2.8% QoQ but declining 3.6% compared with the same period in 2025. Persistent global inflation, rising memory prices, and escalating production costs have continued to weigh on the market, prompting brands to maintain a cautious approach to shipment planning and inventory management.
 TrendForce expects Black Friday and other year-end promotional campaigns to lift TV shipments by 8% QoQ in 4Q26, although volumes will still be down 4% YoY.
 Throughout 2026, soaring memory prices have placed considerable pressure on TV manufacturers' profitability. Brands have sought to cushion the impact of higher production costs by introducing larger screen sizes and upgrading product specifications to raise ASPs. However, these efforts have struggled to offset persistently weak consumer demand. As a result, global TV shipments are forecast to decline 1.4% YoY to 193.48 million units for the full year.
 Looking ahead to 2027, memory prices are expected to remain on an upward trajectory, while display panels and other upstream components face similar cost pressures. Against this backdrop, TrendForce projects that global TV brand shipments will fall another 1.2% YoY to 191.17 million units.
 Samsung retains global shipment lead as Hisense narrows the gap with TCL 
 Samsung retained its leading position in 3Q26 with shipments of 8.4 million units, despite a 1.9% YoY decline. Rising memory costs and subdued market demand weighed particularly heavily on shipments of smaller-screen models, limiting the company's overall growth momentum.
 TCL ranked second with shipments of 7.48 million units, up 1.1% YoY. The company has continued to strengthen its product portfolio through an emphasis on Mini LED technology, larger screen sizes, and mid- to high-end models, which has lifted its product mix and ASPs.
 This strategy has translated into double-digit revenue growth across North America, Europe, and emerging markets, highlighting TCL's success in expanding its international presence.
 Hisense followed closely behind with global TV shipments of 7.45 million units in 3Q26, down 2.7% YoY. With just 30,000 units separating Hisense from TCL, competition between the two leading Chinese brands continues to intensify on the global stage.
 Throughout 2026, Hisense has aggressively expanded its presence in Mini LED and ultra-large-screen TVs. According to its financial disclosures, global sales of TVs measuring 100 inches and above surged 77.4% YoY in the first three quarters, while Mini LED TV sales climbed 75.5% YoY.
 Mini LED TV penetration approaches 15% in 2026, with RGB Mini LED shipments surpassing 2 million units 
 The global Mini LED TV market is entering a period of accelerated expansion. While Chinese brands TCL, Hisense, and Xiaomi have spearheaded adoption over the past several years, Samsung, LG Electronics (LGE), and Sony have broadened their Mini LED product portfolios in 2026, providing a further boost to market growth.
 TrendForce estimates that global Mini LED TV shipments will reach 28.78 million units in 2026, representing a remarkable 116% YoY increase and bringing market penetration close to 15%.
 Samsung is expected to reclaim the top position in global Mini LED TV shipments as it captured 26% market share for the full year. Meanwhile, LGE's accelerated expansion of its Mini LED lineup is projected to propel shipments by more than 800% YoY to 1.75 million units, elevating the company to fourth place worldwide.
 This rapid growth signals a gradual broadening of LGE's premium TV strategy beyond its traditional emphasis on OLED, as the company establishes a stronger foothold in the Mini LED segment.
 Meanwhile, the introduction of RGB Mini LED and Micro RGB TVs by major manufacturers has opened a new front in the competition for the premium TV market.
 Benefiting from its early investment in the technology, Hisense is expected to lead the global RGB Mini LED TV market with a 33% share in 2026, followed by Samsung and Sony in second and third place, respectively. Together, these three brands are projected to account for more than 75% of global shipments.
 TCL, by contrast, has chosen a different technological path for its premium products, focusing on Super Quantum Dot (SQD) technology. By combining blue Mini LED backlighting with quantum dot technology to enhance color performance, TCL is differentiating its approach from RGB Mini LED solutions, which employ red, green, and blue Mini LEDs as backlight sources.
 With leading brands actively promoting these emerging technologies, TrendForce forecasts that global shipments of RGB Mini LED TVs, including Micro RGB models, will surpass 2 million units in 2026.
 This development reflects a broader shift in the premium LCD TV market. Competition is no longer centered solely on Mini LED backlight specifications and the number of local dimming zones, but is increasingly extending to differentiation in backlight architectures and color technologies.

 Mounting Finished-Goods Inventories Prompt Some PC OEMs to Adjust Memory Procurement Plans for 2027, Says TrendForce
 11 November 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 More than a year of rising memory prices has placed mounting cost pressure on the consumer electronics industry, according to TrendForce's latest memory industry research. Notebook shipments, in particular, are expected to decline sharply quarter-over-quarter beginning in 3Q26, leaving PC OEMs grappling with sluggish sales and swelling finished-goods inventories. 
 Against this backdrop, some manufacturers are planning to adjust memory procurement for 4Q26—and even 1Q27—while considering a greater reliance on private-label models in their shipment mix.
 TrendForce notes that PC OEMs brought forward some of their procurement and production schedules to the first half of 2026 in anticipation of further memory price increases. However, higher retail prices have dampened sales across Asia and Europe, while finished-goods inventories have been gradually rising among OEMs and in North American distribution channels.
 Notebook shipments fell 15.8% QoQ in 3Q26, with a further single-digit percentage decline possible in 4Q26. These mounting inventory pressures are prompting some OEMs to reassess their product strategies for 2027, including plans to expand the share of private-label models while incorporating lower-specification memory chips and CPUs with fewer cores.
 PC DRAM contract prices forecast to rise 13–18% QoQ in 4Q26, while client SSD price increases expected to stay below 5% 
 In the PC DRAM market, TrendForce observes that earlier rounds of steep price increases prompted some PC brands to place orders beyond their actual requirements. Overall, declining finished-product shipments have led to a steady increase in DRAM inventory weeks among OEMs since 3Q26, with inventories expected to build further in 4Q26. Some manufacturers have already begun renegotiating their product mix requirements for 2027 with memory suppliers.
 On the supply side, robust demand from AI applications has led memory manufacturers to tentatively plan cuts to PC DRAM supply in 2027. However, suppliers have some flexibility to slightly moderate price increases because there is relatively little pressure to absorb the production capacity involved. Maintaining strategic partnerships with PC customers also remains a priority as manufacturers prepare for longer-term opportunities in edge AI. 
 Against a backdrop of softening PC demand and changing supply strategies, TrendForce forecasts that PC DRAM contract prices will rise 13–18% QoQ in 4Q26, with increases slowing from the previous quarter.
 A similar shift is emerging in the client SSD market, where escalating costs across the entire bill of materials (BOM) have pushed retail prices higher and dampened consumer appetite. As a result, PC OEMs have little choice but to impose strict cost controls on components such as SSDs while firmly resisting additional price increases.
 PC brands have broadly curtailed client SSD procurement in 4Q26 as end-market demand remains subdued and finished-goods inventories stay at elevated levels, purchasing only what is necessary to maintain essential production schedules. This cautious approach is also extending into 1Q27, with procurement plans already being revised downward.
 Meanwhile, client SSD production capacity continues to be squeezed by the growing demands of AI-related applications. Seeking to improve their product mix and production economics, suppliers are imposing steeper price increases on lower-capacity SSDs to discourage demand for these less profitable products.
 In mainstream capacity segments, however, Chinese suppliers and module manufacturers have gained traction by offering comparatively modest price increases, attracting a larger share of orders. Their increasingly competitive quotations have helped soften the broader impact of higher prices maintained by other suppliers.
 As a result, TrendForce expects client SSD contract prices to rise by less than 5% QoQ in 4Q26, marking a notable moderation from the previous quarter.

 Penguin Solutions to Sell Cree LED to Private Equity Firm, Bringing Renewed Attention to the Lighting LED Supply Chain, Says TrendForce
 9 November 2026 
 LED 
 TrendForce 
 Penguin Solutions announced on November 4 that it had entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Cree LED business to private equity firm Transom Capital Group (Transom). 
 Cree LED has long played an important role in the industry as one of the pioneers in bringing LED technology into general lighting applications. TrendForce believes the change in ownership could allow the company to sharpen its focus on its core LED business, with future product strategies likely to emphasize luminous efficacy, cost competitiveness, and comprehensive lighting solutions. The company is also expected to pursue higher-value niche markets, including horticultural lighting.
 Transom, meanwhile, brings extensive experience in corporate carve-outs and operational integration under complex circumstances. However, its approach to integrating Cree LED, along with its future pricing strategies and long-term R&D plans, remains to be seen.
 The transaction will be conducted entirely in cash, although the purchase price has not been disclosed. Subject to customary closing conditions, the deal is expected to be completed in 1Q27. TrendForce notes that Cree LED will emerge as an independently operated LED component company, marking another change in ownership following its earlier sale by Cree, Inc. (now Wolfspeed) to SMART Global Holdings (now Penguin Solutions).
 TrendForce's “2026 Global LED Lighting Market Trends – Database and Vendor Strategies – 2H26” report highlights that Cree LED holds a significant position in the global lighting LED market. The company generated nearly US$200 million in lighting LED revenue in 2025, capturing approximately 5% of the market and climbing to fifth place worldwide. With Samsung LED exiting the market, Cree LED is well positioned to expand its market share further.
 TrendForce highlights Cree LED as one of the few manufacturers in the general lighting LED sector with a comprehensive patent portfolio. Its core business centers on high-efficiency LED chips and high-performance LED components, serving applications ranging from mid- and high-power general lighting to portable lighting, horticultural lighting, and specialty lighting.
 In recent years, Cree LED has refined its product portfolio, broadening its presence across the lighting market while exploring opportunities in applications such as outdoor displays. Lighting applications accounted for 81% of its revenue in the first three quarters of 2026, underscoring their importance as the company’s primary revenue driver.
 These efforts to optimize its product mix and improve cost efficiency have helped Cree LED achieve positive cash flow and steadily strengthen its operating margins, establishing a firmer financial foundation ahead of the sale.
 Another noteworthy development came in August 2026, when private equity firm Gallant Capital provided financial backing to Lumileds. With private equity firms stepping into both Cree LED and Lumileds, the evolving ownership structures and business strategies of major international LED component manufacturers are drawing increasing industry attention. Their next steps are expected to have a lasting influence on the competitive dynamics of the global lighting LED supply chain.

 Persistently High DRAM Prices Drive Adoption of Reballed Memory, with Smartphone Penetration Expected to Reach 7–9% in 2027, Says TrendForce
 6 November 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce's latest memory industry research indicates that the sustained rise in mobile DRAM contract prices is driving smartphone brands to increasingly embrace lower-cost reballed memory components, particularly in entry-level and budget models. TrendForce estimates that the penetration rate of reballed memory in the smartphone market will reach approximately 3–4% in 2026, potentially climbing to 7–9% in 2027.
 TrendForce notes that LPDDR4X 4GB currently accounts for the bulk of reballed memory available in the market, with these components primarily finding their way into 4G smartphones priced below CNY 1,299. Consumers in this segment are highly sensitive to price fluctuations, making affordability a crucial competitive consideration for manufacturers. By incorporating reballed memory, smartphone brands can ease the burden of rising bill of materials (BOM) costs while keeping retail prices competitive.
 However, with DRAM price increases expected to gain further momentum in 1Q27, smartphone manufacturers are likely to face mounting pressure on their cost structures. Against this backdrop, the adoption of lower-specification components and reballed memory could gradually extend into higher price segments, emerging as a key cost-management strategy as brands adapt to a prolonged period of elevated memory prices.
 Despite its growing foothold in the smartphone market, reballed memory remains largely concentrated in entry-level and budget devices. Even as adoption expands in 2027, its share of total annual LPDRAM bit consumption in smartphones is expected to remain relatively modest. As such, the increasing use of reballed components is unlikely to significantly disrupt the prevailing upward trend in DRAM contract prices.
 TrendForce emphasizes that reballed memory provides smartphone brands with an effective means of curbing production costs in the near term, offering much-needed flexibility to sustain shipment volumes amid rising component prices. However, these immediate financial benefits come with notable trade-offs.
 The complexity of sourcing reballed components, coupled with greater uncertainty surrounding quality consistency, can compromise product reliability and potentially shorten device lifespans. Such risks could ultimately erode consumer confidence, tarnish brand reputation, and lead to higher warranty and repair expenses. Manufacturers must therefore strike a careful balance between short-term cost savings and the longer-term implications for product quality and after-sales service costs.

 Marvell’s Acquisition of Lumentum to Unite Optical and Electronic Capabilities, Potentially Challenging Broadcom’s Market Leadership, Says TrendForce
 3 November 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 Marvell has officially announced its acquisition of optical communications giant Lumentum, with both companies’ boards approving the transaction on November 2. The deal remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approval across multiple jurisdictions.
 TrendForce notes that, if completed, the acquisition would significantly strengthen Marvell’s optical technology portfolio and enable the combined company to deliver more comprehensive next-generation optical interconnect solutions. The merger could also reshape the competitive landscape of the optical communications industry, where Broadcom currently holds a commanding position.
 TrendForce estimates that Marvell and Lumentum’s market revenue will rank fourth and eighth, respectively, in the semiconductor wired communications market in 2026. Once the merger is completed, the combined market share will reach nearly 7%, placing the merged company behind only NVIDIA and Broadcom.
 TrendForce explains that Broadcom’s competitive strength in AI optical communications and interconnects stems from its extensive portfolio that spans optical and electronic technologies. Its offerings include Tomahawk switch chips, digital signal processors (DSPs), and optical components such as electro-absorption modulated lasers (EMLs) and continuous-wave (CW) lasers. 
 By comparison, Marvell’s expertise lies primarily in electronic semiconductor technologies, while Lumentum specializes in optical components. Combining these complementary capabilities would create a more formidable competitor with expertise spanning both optical devices and semiconductor ICs, potentially challenging Broadcom’s market leadership.
 TrendForce underscores that the two companies already play important roles in the optical communications supply chain. Lumentum is a key supplier of laser sources, while Marvell provides DSPs and other semiconductor solutions for optical communications applications. If the merger is approved, NVIDIA and other cloud service providers (CSPs) could gain access to a broader range of comprehensive electro-optical interconnect solutions, potentially reducing their reliance on Broadcom while maintaining sourcing flexibility.
 From a technology perspective, TrendForce views the acquisition as a strategic move by Marvell to establish an early foothold in scale-in and scale-up interconnects as the industry transitions toward co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO).
 Incorporating Lumentum’s indium phosphide (InP) laser technology—a critical capability currently missing from its portfolio—would also allow Marvell to integrate its electronic and optical expertise into a more complete optical engine offering.
 Furthermore, the combined company could bring together Marvell’s advanced CMOS chip design, high-speed switching chips, electro-optical interconnects, silicon photonics, and custom XPU capabilities with Lumentum’s high-performance InP lasers, optical transceiver modules, and optical circuit switching (OCS) technologies.
 This would enable the development of integrated solutions spanning chips, optical engines, laser sources, and modules. Through coordinated design and pre-validation, the company could also help customers streamline development and accelerate the adoption of next-generation optical interconnect technologies.
 The acquisition must still secure regulatory approval in the U.S. and China. TrendForce highlights that Chinese optical module makers are among the world’s leading suppliers of 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, relying heavily on Marvell’s DSPs and EML/CW laser sources supplied by companies such as Lumentum.
 The competitive implications are especially significant given Lumentum’s ownership of optical module maker Cloud Light. Chinese optical module makers could face a substantial competitive disadvantage if the merged company were to restrict competitors’ access to critical laser sources, bundle DSPs with laser products, or prioritize shipments to its own subsidiaries.  
 As a result, TrendForce expects the potential impact of the merger on the competitive position and long-term viability of Chinese optical module suppliers to be a central consideration in China’s regulatory review.

 AI Networking and Interconnect Market Projected to Reach US$279.8 Billion in 2027, with Scale-Up Share Rising to 24%, Says TrendForce
 2 November 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce's latest AI infrastructure research indicates that the continued expansion of AI server clusters and surging accelerator bandwidth requirements are fueling rapid growth in the global AI networking and interconnect market. Market revenue is projected to climb from US$37.9 billion in 2024 to US$279.8 billion in 2027, representing a CAGR of 95% over the period.
 Back-end network switches and optical transceivers have traditionally been the primary growth engines. However, market momentum is increasingly extending to high-speed accelerator interconnects and network interface cards. Looking ahead, the shipment mix and network topologies adopted by different AI chip platforms will play a pivotal role in determining both the market's overall size and how value is distributed across the supply chain.
 Switches are expected to remain the largest revenue contributor, generating US$105 billion in 2027 and accounting for nearly 38% of the market. Network interface cards and data processing units (NICs/DPUs) are also poised for robust growth, supported by higher deployment volumes and bandwidth upgrades across next-generation platforms. Revenue from these products is forecast to more than double YoY to US$57.4 billion in 2027.
 Meanwhile, continued migration toward higher-speed specifications is expected to lift pluggable optical transceiver revenue to US$84.1 billion in 2027. Together, switches, NICs/DPUs, and pluggable optical transceivers will account for approximately 88% of total AI networking and interconnect revenue.
 Among interconnect segments, high-speed connections between AI accelerators, known as scale-up networking, are seeing the fastest revenue growth. As GPU platforms evolve toward rack-scale architectures, accelerator interconnects are expanding beyond server motherboards into dedicated switch trays, creating additional demand for switching equipment and copper cables. 
 Based on AI cluster deployment estimates, TrendForce projects that scale-up networking's share of AI networking and interconnect revenue will grow from 11% in 2024 to 24% in 2027. Copper cables are expected to remain the dominant interconnect medium within GPU racks in 2027. Google, however, is already scaling its TPU clusters with optical interconnects through its Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI) technology, alongside optical circuit switches (OCS).
 Scale-out networking, which connects servers across AI clusters, remains the largest interconnect segment by revenue. Ongoing bandwidth upgrades are expected to shift the primary revenue driver for pluggable optical transceivers from 800G to 1.6T products in 2027.
 Despite the continued decline in the average selling price (ASP) of 1.6T transceivers as production scales up, these products are still expected to command more than twice the price of their 800G counterparts. Consequently, the growing share of higher-speed products in the shipment mix will continue to bolster overall market revenue. TrendForce forecasts that pluggable optical transceiver revenue will surge 76% YoY in 2027, outpacing shipment growth, with 1.6T products contributing approximately 56% of pluggable transceiver revenue.
 Importantly, growth in AI chip shipments will not translate proportionally into networking revenue. The networking value associated with each accelerator varies according to the interconnect topology, switch configuration, and NIC bandwidth requirements of the underlying AI platform.
 Emerging optical connectivity technologies and network architectures are also lifting overall market revenue. Co-packaged optics (CPO) and OCSs, for example, address distinct interconnect requirements. By integrating optical engines and switch chips within a single package, CPO shifts a portion of the optical component value traditionally captured by pluggable transceivers into switching equipment. OCS, meanwhile, enables large-scale cluster interconnectivity through optical circuit switching.
 Overall, TrendForce expects the distribution of value across the AI networking and interconnect supply chain to continue evolving as AI platform configurations diversify and optical interconnect architectures advance.

 New MacBook Pro Enters Market; Global OLED Notebook Shipments Forecast to Grow Over 40% YoY in 2027, Says TrendForce
 29 October 2026 
 Display 
 /
 Consumer Electronics 
 TrendForce 
 Apple’s newly unveiled MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display marks a significant milestone in the evolution of MacBook display technology and user experience, becoming the first model in the lineup to feature a tandem OLED touchscreen. 
 TrendForce estimates that shipments of the new model will reach 1.2–1.5 million units in 2027. Apple’s entry into the OLED notebook market is also providing fresh impetus for panel makers to accelerate the development of advanced display technologies.
 However, TrendForce notes that the new MacBook Pro’s premium starting price of US$2,899 for the 14-inch model, coupled with its initial availability alongside existing Mini-LED models, could temper near-term replacement demand. 
 Nevertheless, the launch further reinforces Apple’s reputation for technological innovation and premium positioning. Together with the MacBook Neo’s departure from Apple’s traditional entry-level pricing strategy, the move reflects the company’s broader efforts to expand its product portfolio across a wider spectrum of price points.
 Until now, the OLED notebook market has been driven primarily by Windows-based brands such as Lenovo, HP, and ASUS, which have gradually expanded their OLED offerings across different price segments. Apple’s arrival is expected to give the market additional momentum, encouraging brands to prioritize OLED models in their product roadmaps while strengthening consumer acceptance of the technology. This, in turn, could pave the way for broader OLED adoption in notebook displays.
 Despite an anticipated contraction in the overall notebook market for two consecutive years, TrendForce forecasts that OLED notebook shipments will grow nearly 40% YoY in 2026, followed by another increase of more than 40% in 2027.
 Samsung Display secures exclusive supply position as rivals set their sights on the OLED MacBook Air 
 Samsung Display (SDC) is currently the exclusive panel supplier for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. The company has designated Phase 1 of its G8.6 A6 production line at its Asan campus in South Korea as a dedicated facility for Apple.
 The new MacBook Pro carries considerable strategic significance as the first product to enter mass production on SDC’s G8.6 fine metal mask (FMM) OLED line. Its selection as the display for Apple’s first and most premium OLED notebook underscores SDC’s technological capabilities and strengthens its position at the forefront of the OLED market.
 TrendForce explains that the new MacBook Pro’s tandem OLED architecture and pixel density of 254 pixels per inch (PPI) impose exceptionally demanding requirements on panel production. Meeting these specifications presents substantial challenges for suppliers, particularly in terms of material costs and manufacturing yields.
 Although other panel makers are conducting qualification programs, the high cost of meeting Apple’s stringent specifications, combined with SDC’s established position as the primary supplier, presents considerable barriers to entry. As a result, competing OLED panel makers, including LG Display, BOE, and TCL CSOT, are largely directing their efforts toward securing a place in the supply chain for the OLED MacBook Air, which is expected to debut in 2029.

 AI Inference Drives CPU and DDR5 Demand, with High-Capacitance MLCC Shortages Expected to Persist Through 1H27, Says TrendForce
 29 October 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce's latest MLCC industry research shows that the rapid evolution of AI applications from model training to inference and AI agents is driving a new wave of CPU demand. Since each CPU requires accompanying power modules and DDR5 memory, the proliferation of these components is driving a substantial increase in high-capacitance MLCC requirements across CPU motherboards and memory modules. This is placing mounting pressure on the supply of standard high-capacitance MLCCs.
 Shipments of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform are expected to ramp up month by month beginning in 4Q26, and AMD is starting to procure specialized high-capacitance MLCCs for its MI450 platform. As a result, ODMs anticipate that shortages of high-end MLCCs will be most severe in 1Q27 and 2Q27.
 In stark contrast, the consumer electronics market continues to grapple with subdued demand as AI applications command a growing share of production capacity, pushing up the cost of memory and other critical components, and, in turn, driving end-product prices higher.
 TrendForce’s research indicates major notebook ODMs expect orders to decline by an average of 10–15% YoY in 4Q26, while smartphone brands are similarly scaling back shipments of entry-level and midrange models.
 Spot prices for low- to mid-capacitance consumer-grade MLCCs slipped approximately 5% in early October before finding a temporary floor, while price increases for high-end specifications have begun to lose momentum. Nevertheless, supply constraints remain pronounced for AI-grade MLCCs, with shortages now extending to communications-grade components used in optical communication modules.
 Adding to these supply-side pressures is the persistent rise in material and logistics costs. Japan’s import price index, for instance, surged 24.5% YoY in September, with nickel, copper, and silver—essential materials used in MLCC electrodes—especially exposed to escalating costs.
 Murata executives have acknowledged that existing production capacity falls far short of market requirements, prompting the company to bring forward its expansion plans. However, even with this accelerated investment, new capacity is unlikely to come online before 2028, leaving little prospect of meaningful near-term supply relief.
 TrendForce expects the high-end MLCC shortage to extend through 1H27, allowing suppliers to retain the upper hand in pricing negotiations. With discussions over 1Q27 price scheduled to begin in November 2026, Japanese manufacturers appear increasingly likely to follow Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO) in implementing price increases. Meanwhile, Taiwanese and Chinese suppliers are expected to keep benefiting from spillover orders for consumer-grade MLCCs.

 iPhone Duo Launch Sparks Strong Demand, but Fold-Area Structural Reliability and Hardware–Software Integration Remain Challenges, Says TrendForce
 28 October 2026 
 Display 
 /
 Consumer Electronics 
 TrendForce 
 Less than a week after Apple opened preorders for its first foldable smartphone—the iPhone Duo—its official website was already showing delivery dates extending into January 2027 for some orders.
 According to TrendForce, initial user feedback has been polarized. While users have praised the split-screen functionality and viewing experience when the device is unfolded, black borders in some apps, button placement, and fingerprint authentication have added to the learning curve.
 Reports of damaged displays and high repair estimates have also shifted attention toward product reliability and long-term ownership costs. Given the Duo’s premium positioning, the key question for consumers is whether its expanded screen space delivers a sufficiently compelling overall experience to justify the price.
 TrendForce estimates that global foldable smartphone shipments will edge up just 0.5% in 2026. Apple’s first foldable iPhone is expected to ship approximately 5 million units, accounting for about 24.8% of the market in 2026. With the overall market remaining largely flat, Apple’s entry is poised to accelerate shifts in market share among competing brands.
 One of the Duo’s defining features is its barely visible display crease. TrendForce explains that a foldable OLED display consists of multiple layers, including cover materials, optical adhesives, display components, and encapsulation structures. These layers experience different tensile, compressive, and shear stresses as the display folds. Managing these stresses requires careful optimization of the bending radius, layer thicknesses, and elastic moduli, while allowing controlled slippage within the display stack through the adhesive layers.
 These measures reduce strain on functional layers and improve the display’s recovery when unfolded. Nanoscale surface textures also scatter reflected light, making the reflective band along the fold less noticeable. By addressing structural deformation and optical appearance, respectively, these approaches improve perceived brightness uniformity across the crease.
 The Duo’s teardrop hinge plays a critical role in dynamically controlling display support and clearance. When unfolded, the hinge keeps the display flat and provides the stability for touch input. When closed, it creates the space needed for the panel to fold along its intended curvature.
 One hypothesis arising from recent teardown analyses of damaged Duo displays is that insufficient retraction of the central support during folding may cause unintended contact and localized stress concentrations. Apple has provided replacements for a small number of devices exhibiting inner-display abnormalities. From an engineering perspective, further improvements would likely center on coordinated control of hinge travel, support height, bonding precision, and assembly tolerances.
 The Duo also brings a larger workspace to a portable form factor, allowing users to read documents, review AI-generated summaries, and edit content simultaneously. Translating this additional screen space into meaningful productivity gains requires apps to dynamically adapt their layouts as the device opens and closes, while preserving reading positions, text input, and ongoing tasks. Some apps still display black borders or fail to make full use of the available screen area, indicating that software adaptation has yet to fully capitalize on the hardware’s capabilities.
 The larger display also places greater demands on power management. Although lowering the refresh rate can reduce some display-driving power consumption, the power required for OLED light emission still depends on brightness, emitting area, and displayed content. Even a static document with a white background continues to consume power.
 Balancing large-screen multitasking, AI processing, and battery life therefore requires a combination of more efficient emissive materials, optimized optical structures, and adaptive display-driving technologies.
 TrendForce notes that Apple’s greatest advantage lies in its ability to integrate chips, operating systems, and its developer ecosystem. As app compatibility and hardware reliability improve, the Duo is expected to further expand the practical value of foldable displays, helping shift competition in the foldable smartphone market from form-factor innovation toward multitasking efficiency.

 Server CPU Shipments Projected to Grow Over 40% YoY in 2027, with Arm-Based Products Continuing to Gain Market Share, Says TrendForce
 22 October 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce’s latest AI server industry research indicates that demand for server CPUs has grown steadily since the second half of 2025 as AI service providers actively introduce AI agent applications. Server CPU shipments are projected to increase 31% YoY in 2026. 
 In 2027, continued growth in AI inference demand and rising adoption of agentic AI services are expected to drive server CPU shipments up by more than 40% YoY, potentially reshaping a market landscape traditionally dominated by x86 processors.
 TrendForce notes that the emergence of AI agents is expected to increase the share of AI inference workloads in cloud data centers, gradually changing the ratio of CPUs to GPUs/ASICs within servers. Based on server rack configurations planned by major providers and their anticipated growth trajectories, the CPU-to-GPU/ASIC ratio is expected to shift from the traditional 1:8 toward 1:2—or even 1:1—providing additional momentum for server CPU shipments.
 The x86 segment, led by Intel and AMD, accounted for nearly 90% of the server CPU market in 2025, with AMD already gaining share. Arm-based processors, meanwhile, had only recently surpassed 10% of the market. Both x86 and Arm CPU suppliers are aggressively increasing shipments in 2026 to capitalize on opportunities driven by AI inference demand. 
 However, process and packaging challenges with Intel’s new products have delayed shipments. The company continues to rely on its existing Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids product lines, while limited internal manufacturing capacity constrains overall shipment growth and prevents it from fully meeting customer orders. This has contributed to a decline in market share.
 AMD’s next-generation Venice processors entered small-scale mass production in 2026, although its existing Genoa and Turin platforms remain the primary shipment drivers. Despite tight capacity at TSMC limiting AMD’s ability to accommodate additional orders, TrendForce estimates that the company’s share of the server CPU market will increase significantly to approximately 27% in 2026.
 In the Arm-based CPU segment, AWS continues to deploy its internally developed Graviton processors, while demand for NVIDIA’s Grace CPUs continues to expand. Google’s in-house Axion CPUs have entered high-volume shipments, and Microsoft’s Cobalt 100 and Arm’s internally developed AGI processors have also entered mass production and shipment. These developments are expected to drive faster shipment growth for Arm-based CPUs than for x86 products in 2026, pushing their share of the server CPU market above 20%.
 TrendForce expects Arm-based CPUs to capture approximately 30% of the server CPU market in 2027. Growth will be driven primarily by a substantial ramp-up in NVIDIA Vera CPU shipments, alongside high-volume production of new processors from Google, AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, Arm, and Huawei, as well as Alibaba’s introduction of new Yitian 720/730 CPUs.
 Within the x86 segment, Intel’s next-generation products are expected to remain in limited supply, while AMD is projected to maintain more stable shipments. AMD's market share is expected to increase further as the company plans to launch new products in the first half of 2027.

 Optical Fiber Spot Prices Surge Severalfold in 2026, with Data Center-Driven Supply Shortages Expected to Persist Through 2028, Says TrendForce
 19 October 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 /
 Telecommunications 
 TrendForce 
 AI data centers, data center interconnects, and high-capacity backbone network deployments are driving rising demand for optical fiber. According to TrendForce’s latest telecommunications industry research, this is expected to lead to a global supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026. 
 Tightening supply is projected to push spot prices for finished optical fiber products to 2.8–5 times their 2025 levels or higher. In response, telecom operators are shifting from short-term purchasing to long-term supply agreements (LTAs) to lock in fiber supply early.
 TrendForce notes that substantial demand from AI data center-related applications has tightened global optical fiber supply since late 2025, with shortages expected to persist until at least 2028. 
 On the supply side, global optical fiber capacity utilization has climbed to 92% in 2026, while inventory levels have fallen from four months in 2024 to just one month. Some leading suppliers are already booked into the first quarter of 2027, indicating that existing production capacity is running close to full.
 Meanwhile, expanding optical fiber preform capacity requires installing deposition equipment and establishing production processes, typically taking 18–24 months. Even with expansions in the planning stage, new capacity will take time to come online, limiting meaningful supply growth in the near term.
 Global optical fiber demand is estimated to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers in 2026, driven primarily by data center construction, which accounts for roughly 18–20% of the total. That share is projected to rise to 30–35% in 2027. Beyond continued AI data center expansion by hyperscale CSPs, chipmakers and telecom operators are also investing in related infrastructure, further lifting fiber demand for data center interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks.
 TrendForce’s research shows that the widening supply-demand imbalance has driven a sharp increase in spot quotations for finished optical fiber products. For example, the average price of bend-insensitive fiber (BIF) used for cabling within data centers is expected to average more than five times its 2025 level in 2026. 
 Prices for AI backbone fiber used in data center interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks are projected to reach approximately 2.8 times their 2025 levels, while quotations for mainstream telecom fiber are expected to rise to around 3.7 times their previous levels.
 Telecom operators are increasingly turning to long-term agreements (LTAs) to secure future fiber requirements as supply conditions continue to tighten. In September 2026, Verizon and Corning signed a multi-year supply agreement covering 129 million fiber-kilometers (approximately 80 million fiber-miles) of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions for delivery between 2027 and 2032. The fiber will support broadband deployments as well as high-capacity backbone networks connecting AI data centers.
 TrendForce believes the current optical fiber shortage differs from past telecom infrastructure cycles, as it stems from sustained growth in incremental demand tied to AI data centers. With supply unable to scale quickly in the near term and demand continuing to grow steadily, using LTAs to lock in fiber supply early are expected to become increasingly common among telecom operators and large infrastructure providers.

 Meta and Chinese Brands Drive Doubling of AR Glasses Shipments, 2026 Forecast Expected to Reach 1.31 Million Units, Says TrendForce
 15 October 2026 
 Emerging Technologies 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce’s latest report, “2026 Near-Eye Display Market Trends and Technology Analysis,” highlights how AR glasses are gradually transitioning from proof-of-concept products to the consumer market. Stronger-than-expected growth momentum for Meta’s Ray-Ban Display glasses has drawn more consumer attention to AR glasses, prompting brands and supply chain players to accelerate product development. 
 Other AR glasses brands, benefiting from the spillover effects of Meta's success, are expanding their product portfolios and sales channels to capture early consumer interest before other technology giants fully enter the market. TrendForce forecasts global AR glasses shipments to surge from 620,000 units in 2025 to 1.31 million units in 2026, marking 111.1% YoY growth.
 Meta is expected to maintain its lead in 2026 with approximately 20% of global shipments. The other four major brands—XREAL, Even Realities, Rokid, and RayNeo—are projected to account for a combined 53.2%, indicating that brands beyond Meta have also established a substantial market presence.
 XREAL focuses on AR glasses designed for entertainment and media consumption. Its Aura glasses, developed in collaboration with Google, are scheduled to launch by the end of 2026, further strengthening the brand's product portfolio and market influence. Even Realities specializes in information-display AR glasses, emphasizing lightweight designs and aesthetics that improve the wearing experience. Rokid and RayNeo offer diverse product portfolios tailored to different consumer use cases. 
 Together, the five leading brands are expanding their offerings and reaching broader consumer segments, serving as the primary drivers behind global AR glasses shipments surpassing one million units in 2026.
 TrendForce notes that as AR glasses shipments reach new highs, OLEDoS and LEDoS are expected to account for approximately 80% of the market combined. 
 OLEDoS is projected to maintain a slight lead thanks to its widespread adoption in entertainment-oriented AR glasses. However, its applications across other product categories remain limited. As a result, OLEDoS developers are revisiting monochrome green display configurations to penetrate the information-display segment, seeking new outlets for the substantial production capacity expected to come online.
 LEDoS, valued for its lightweight advantages, remains the key display technology driving the adoption of information-display AR glasses. Nevertheless, achieving full-color displays is expected to remain a significant technical challenge in the near term. To address the limitations of monochrome green displays, supply chain players are developing dual-color red-and-green solutions. By improving visual differentiation and information readability, these solutions aim to extend LEDoS applications to more advanced use cases. 
 As LEDoS and OLEDoS continue to improve their display specifications and expand into new applications, while LCoS adoption grows through Meta's products, AR glasses brands will have access to a wider range of technology options and greater flexibility in managing costs. These developments are expected to drive further product innovation and application expansion, with global AR glasses shipments projected to grow by nearly 80% in 2027.

 CSP CapEx Projected to Exceed US$1.5 Trillion in 2027, with AI Server Revenue Growing Over 90% YoY on Higher Shipments and Prices, Says TrendForce
 14 October 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 Hyperscale CSPs are ramping up investments in servers and AI infrastructure, according to TrendForce’s latest AI server industry research. Combined CapEx among the world’s nine leading CSPs is projected to surge 106% YoY to US$957 billion in 2026. In 2027, this figure is expected to surpass $1.5 trillion, representing a further 60% YoY increase. Both forecasts have been revised upward from previous estimates.
 The world’s nine leading CSPs consist of Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, ByteDance, Tencent, Alibaba, and Baidu. The upward revision to their combined 2027 CapEx growth forecast—from 50% to 60%—reflects three key factors: rising prices for complete server systems, higher component quotations amid supply shortages, and advance payments required by some component suppliers to secure supply, prompting CSPs to bring forward cash expenditures.
 Strong financial resources fuel AI server procurement, with shipment growth expected to approach 36% in 2027 
 Demand for AI servers continues to strengthen as CSP investment remains robust. Beyond hyperscale CSPs, Tier-2 data center operators such as Tesla and CoreWeave have also continued purchasing AI servers. TrendForce now forecasts AI server shipments to grow 32.2% YoY in 2026 given the strong overall demand outlook.
 Looking ahead to 2027, hyperscale CSPs are expected to remain the primary drivers of the AI market. Additional demand from neocloud providers, sovereign AI projects, and LLM developers introducing new AI models and application services will further support procurement momentum. Consequently, AI server shipments are projected to increase by nearly 36% YoY.
 In terms of market value, AI servers are expected to generate approximately $479 billion in revenue in 2026, supported by their high ASPs and solid shipment performance. This would account for nearly 75% of the projected $639.2 billion in total server market revenue, which includes both general-purpose and AI servers.
 In 2027, end-customer orders are expected to center on rack-scale solutions such as NVIDIA's GB300 and VR200, as well as AMD's Helios series. Shortages and rising prices of key components, particularly memory, are driving up the ASPs of next-generation AI server racks.
 TrendForce therefore expects total server market revenue to surpass $1 trillion for the first time in 2027, while AI server revenue is projected to surge by more than 90% YoY to nearly $920 billion. This means that AI servers' share of total server market revenue is expected to rise to approximately 81%.

 Integrated Optical-Electrical Testing Platforms Become Key to CPO Mass Production, Reshaping the Test Equipment Supply Chain, Says TrendForce
 13 October 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce’s latest research on AI interconnect technologies reveals that growing demand for high-speed transmission in AI data centers is accelerating the transition of co-packaged optics (CPO) toward mass production, making shorter test times and lower costs increasingly important. Furthermore, demand for integrated test equipment and software is rising as CPO requires coordinated electrical and optical measurements.
 TrendForce expects 2027 to be a pivotal year for the convergence of CPO testing architectures. While established automated test equipment (ATE) suppliers are expanding their presence in this market, new manufacturing processes and technical challenges are also creating opportunities for equipment, test interface, and semiconductor assembly and test service providers.
 CPO combines optical engines with switching or computing chips in a single package. One key challenge in mass production is ensuring precise optical coupling, which depends on alignment module suppliers equipped with multi-axis control. When combined with position feedback and optical search algorithms, these tools enable optical coupling and testing equipment to achieve faster and more stable alignment. 
 Although optical alignment times have already decreased to the second or even sub-second level, a complete test of a single photonic integrated circuit (PIC) can still take over 100 seconds. Consequently, the bottleneck in mass production is now shifting from alignment accuracy to testing speed.
 CPO testing currently requires multiple instruments, including laser sources, optical switches, optical power meters, and optical spectrum analyzers. Coordinating instrument control, calibration, and test procedures therefore becomes more complex with functions and suppliers spread across different equipment categories. Additionally, each instrument is used for a different length of time during testing. 
 Equipping every test station with a complete set of instruments can leave some expensive equipment underutilized, driving up costs. The key to optical-electrical test integration lies in using unified software to coordinate electrical and optical measurements, supported by optical path switching and instrument sharing across multiple test stations to improve equipment utilization. 
 As CPO moves toward mass production, the ability to integrate different instruments effectively on a single platform will be critical to reducing costs and increasing throughput.
 Competition shifts toward platform integration as suppliers expand their CPO testing capabilities 
 TrendForce identifies seven major segments in the CPO testing supply chain: ATE, probing and test interfaces, optical and high-speed measurement instruments, test integration and automation, core optical coupling and alignment modules, third-party testing and analysis, and packaging and production testing. Responsibilities across these segments continue to overlap.
 Leading traditional ATE suppliers have increased investment in response to customer demand. Teradyne acquired Quantifi Photonics in 2025 to strengthen its optical measurement capabilities. Advantest is integrating optical instruments through its existing test platforms and software. In September 2026, the company announced a collaboration with VIAVI and SENKO to combine automated testing, optical measurement, and detachable optical interfaces. The partners subsequently demonstrated a simulated production testing workflow for CPO modules at ECOC 2026.
 These developments indicate that industry value is gradually shifting from individual instrument performance to the ability to integrate complete production testing platforms. Further advances in instrument sharing across test stations and parallel testing of multiple devices could help reduce testing costs per unit.
 TrendForce observes that Taiwanese suppliers have established a presence across several segments of the CPO testing supply chain. GMT Global provides multi-axis optical coupling and alignment modules, while MPI offers probing equipment and optical alignment solutions. WinWay specializes in test interfaces, and Chroma has capabilities in automated testing and burn-in testing.
 Third-party testing providers, including MSS, MA-tek, and iST, are helping customers accelerate product development through optical-electrical measurements, materials analysis, failure analysis, and reliability verification. Packaging and testing providers such as ASE can further bridge the gap between packaging processes and production testing, extending the potential benefits across both equipment and service suppliers.
 Chinese suppliers are leveraging their existing experience in optical communications manufacturing and testing to accelerate the localization of test equipment. For example, Semight Instruments has introduced a 65 GHz sampling oscilloscope and begun volume shipments, indicating progress in certain high-speed measurement technologies. 
 Nevertheless, China still relies heavily on imports for high-end measurement instruments overall. It also remains to be seen whether experience in optical module testing can be extended to complete CPO mass production platforms. Customer adoption, testing efficiency, and long-term stability will be key factors to monitor. 
 RoboTechnik completed its full acquisition of Germany-based ficonTEC in 2025, gaining a foothold in the global optoelectronic packaging and test equipment supply chain. Whether this ownership change will influence procurement decisions among European and U.S. customers will be another important development to watch.
 TrendForce expects 2027 to be a pivotal year for the convergence of CPO testing architectures and equipment investment strategies, while 2028 will serve as a critical period for validating readiness for large-scale mass production. Suppliers that can integrate different test equipment and provide production-scale services are expected to strengthen their strategic positions in the supply chain as customers place greater emphasis on testing efficiency, quality, and cost.

 Rising Costs Threaten Notebook Demand in 2027, Raising Risks of Shipment Declines and Price Increases, Says TrendForce
 8 October 2026 
 Consumer Electronics 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce's latest notebook industry research reveals that the primary risk facing the market in 2027 is expected to shift from supply constraints to the impact of rising costs on demand. Global notebook shipments are currently projected to decline by a low-single-digit percentage in 2027. 
 However, if DRAM and CPU prices remain elevated, brands may be forced to pass more of these costs on to consumers. These higher retail prices could further extend replacement cycles, potentially pushing the full-year shipment decline into the high-single-digit range.
 In 2026, improved CPU availability, early procurement by brands, and the pull-forward of some replacement demand helped support notebook shipments. However, this does not indicate a meaningful recovery in end-market demand. 
 With some purchases originally expected in the second half of 2026 and beyond already brought forward, replacement momentum in subsequent periods is likely to weaken. Furthermore, as lower-cost inventories are gradually depleted, brands will face more direct pressure from rising CPU, DRAM, and SSD prices.
 TrendForce notes that for a mainstream notebook with a manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) of US$900, CPU, DRAM, and SSD components accounted for approximately 68% of the bill of materials (BOM) cost in 3Q26. This highlights the growing influence of core component costs on product pricing.
 Brands consequently face difficult trade-offs. Raising retail prices risks weakening demand, while absorbing higher costs would squeeze gross margins. Alternatively, reducing specifications such as memory capacity to control BOM costs could undermine product competitiveness. 
 In 2027, brands are therefore unlikely to be able to maintain pricing, specifications, and profitability simultaneously. The extent to which they pass higher costs on to consumers will be a key factor shaping demand.
 Higher costs in emerging manufacturing locations prompt brands to reassess production strategies 
 Against this backdrop, notebook brands may reconsider production strategies previously adjusted to mitigate geopolitical risks. If tariff pressures do not intensify further, the factors guiding manufacturing glocalization are likely to shift from minimizing policy risks toward production costs, supply-chain completeness, and operational efficiency.
 With component prices remaining elevated, the additional logistics, component sourcing, and supply-chain management costs associated with emerging manufacturing locations will come under greater scrutiny. This could encourage brands to relocate some capacity previously established outside China for risk diversification back to the country.
 TrendForce estimates that the share of global notebook production outside China will decline from approximately 24% in 2025 to 21% in 2026, potentially falling below 20% in 2027. This suggests that brands are reassessing the balance between supply-chain diversification and manufacturing efficiency as policy and cost conditions evolve.
 In 2027, supply conditions for notebook components may become more uneven. DRAM supply is likely to stay tight as AI server applications continue to absorb advanced-process capacity, while PC DRAM faces the risk of limited supply growth. Conversely, NAND Flash supply constraints might ease in the second half of 2027 with new capacity coming online. 
 Outside memory, components like PCBs, MLCCs, and PMICs are also under pressure due to capacity allocation decisions, raw material costs, and geopolitical issues. These challenges could result in higher prices or longer lead times, increasing brands’ cost burdens and complicating supply-chain management.
 TrendForce indicates that the focus of the notebook market in 2027 will shift from whether sufficient components are available to whether consumers can absorb higher prices. If brands can mitigate the impact on retail prices by adjusting product mixes and specifications while absorbing some of the additional costs, the shipment decline could remain in the low-single-digit range.
 Conversely, if component costs continue to rise and are fully passed on to consumers, demand could weaken further, pushing the full-year shipment decline into the high-single-digit range. Brands’ ability to strike a new balance among pricing, specifications, supply stability, and profitability will be critical to stabilizing the notebook market in 2027.

 Six Leading Suppliers Bet on VCSEL NPO; VCSEL Demand Projected to Reach 650 Million Units by 2031, Says TrendForce
 8 October 2026 
 Semiconductors 
 /
 LED 
 TrendForce 
 TrendForce’s latest report, “2027 Infrared Sensing and Optical Communication Market Trend”, shows that rapidly growing demand for data transmission in expanding data center networks is increasing interest in VCSEL-based near-packaged optics (NPO). This technology is favored for its low power usage, easier maintenance, and a mature supply chain. Major companies like Lumentum, Furukawa Electric, Coherent, Broadcom, ams OSRAM, and HiSilicon are investing heavily in R&D. 
 Several VCSEL NPO solutions are expected to launch between 2027 and 2028. Coupled with rising demand for short-reach optical transceivers, this trend is projected to boost VCSEL sales to 650 million units by 2031, growing at a CAGR of 38% from 2025 to 2031.
 In scale-up network architectures for AI data centers, active electrical cables (AECs) primarily rely on multiple retimers to mitigate data loss and signal attenuation. However, as transmission speeds advance into the 1.6 Tbps era, high-frequency electrical signal attenuation over copper cables increases significantly. This is expected to accelerate the transition toward optical interconnect technologies for short-reach transmission, including architectures such as VCSEL NPO and Micro LED CPO.
 Looking at supplier strategies, Lumentum, Furukawa Electric, Coherent, Broadcom, ams OSRAM, and HiSilicon are developing VCSEL NPO solutions to capture future opportunities in scale-up networks. Coherent, Broadcom, ams OSRAM, and HiSilicon are adopting mature 850nm VCSELs paired with photodiodes to achieve aggregate bandwidth of up to 3.2 Tbps, though chromatic dispersion will limit further improvements in transmission distance and bandwidth.
 Lumentum and Furukawa Electric have adopted higher-cost 1,060nm VCSEL solutions, while Coherent is also planning to adopt this approach. They offer extremely high fiber-coupling efficiency, low dispersion, low relative intensity noise (RIN), and strong performance at elevated operating temperatures, making them better suited to future increases in transmission speeds.
 TrendForce notes that Micro LED CPO and VCSEL NPO require arrays of emitters and receivers to be integrated with ASICs/GPUs to achieve ultra-low power consumption and extremely high transmission density. Although Micro LED CPO offers long-term potential to approach the theoretical limit of energy consumption per bit, the technology continues to face challenges involving mass transfer, optical fiber compatibility, and coupling efficiency. Its supply chain also remains under development.
 Compared with Micro LED CPO, VCSEL NPO offers more mature commercial conditions in terms of power consumption per bit, maintenance flexibility, and supply-chain readiness. Both 850 nm and 1,060 nm solutions can address the high-density transmission requirements of AI data centers. By offering a balance between performance and practical feasibility, VCSEL NPO has emerged as a highly competitive option for scale-up optical interconnect architectures at this stage.
 Future VCSEL NPO development will focus on further improving overall performance. On the optical side, suppliers will seek to optimize the combination of VCSEL wavelengths and optical fiber technologies. At the chip level, development will focus on increasing the data rate of individual VCSELs from 100G to the 200G standard, as well as developing smaller Micro VCSELs with individual device sizes of 100–200 µm. Higher-density, multi-channel arrays can then be used to further increase transmission bandwidth.
 Overall, continued improvements in performance, technology maturity, and supply-chain readiness are strengthening the competitive advantages of VCSEL NPO and accelerating the development of barriers to entry around the technology.
